rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording does not establish a vow: it can mean a promise to meet legally required expenditures if God grants wealth; zakat itself arises from owning the threshold for a year.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أن اللفظ لا يدل عليه ، لأن المذكور في اللفظ ليس إلا قوله : { لئن ءاتانا من فضله لنصدقن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the future-tense promise does not require immediate performance, it can cover obligatory payments when they later fall due, including zakat required by law.
rows.anchor: قلنا : قوله : { لنصدقن } لا يوجب أنهم يفعلون ذلك على الفور ، لأن هذا إخبار عن إيقاع هذا الفعل فس المستقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi cites an earlier report that the passage was revealed about people who refused to pay zakat.
rows.anchor: ويتأكد ذلك بما روينا أن هذه الآية إنما نزلت في حق من امتنع من أداء الزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God granting them bounty means receiving wealth by any route, including trade, production, or another means.
rows.anchor: المراد إيتاء المال بأي طريق كان ، سواء كان بطريق التجارة ، أو بطريق الاستنتاج أو بغيرهما

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj derives the form from لنتصدقن, with the tāʾ assimilated into ṣād because the letters are close.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : الأصل لنتصدقن . ولكن التاء أدغمت في الصاد لقربها منها

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says al-muṣaddiq is the giver and al-mutasaddiq the asker.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : المصدق المعطي والمتصدق السائل

rows.speaker: الأصمعي والفراء
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī and al-Farrāʾ reject al-Layth’s distinction: al-mutasaddiq is the giver, as Yusuf 12:88 shows.
rows.anchor: قال الأصمعي والفراء : هذا خطأ فالمتصدق هو المعطي قال تعالى : { وتصدق علينا إن الله يجزى المتصدقين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous person is the opposite of the corrupt person: one who fulfills what religious duty requires, whereas the corrupt withholds it.
rows.anchor: الصالح ضد المفسد ، والمفسد عبارة عن الذي بخل بما يلزمه في التكليف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that Thaʿlaba promised God to give charity and fulfill his pledge if God opened the doors of good to him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : كان ثعلبة قد عاهد الله تعالى لئن فتح الله عليه أبواب الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says the restriction in the reported formulation lacks evidence: the first promise points to obligatory zakat, the second to every kind of legally obligatory payment.
rows.anchor: وأقول التقييد لا دليل عليه . بل قوله : { لنصدقن } إشارة إلى إخراج الزكاة الواجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi identifies three traits: miserliness, meaning withholding a right; turning away from the pledge; and disregarding God's duties and commands.
rows.anchor: وصفهم بصفات ثلاثة : الصفة الأولى : البخل وهو عبارة عن منع الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi assigns the causing of hypocrisy to God: good deeds cannot cause it, while omissions are nonbeing, occur without hypocrisy, and would cause kufr even if lawful; the causal wording of 9:77 also rules them out.
rows.anchor: فثبت بهذه الوجوه أنه لا يجوز إسناد هذا الإعقاب إلى شيء من الأشياء التي تقدم ذكرها إلا إلى الله سبحانه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that after they went astray in the past, God led them farther from religion in the future.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج إن معناه : أنهم لما ضلوا في الماضي ، فهو تعالى أضلهم عن الدين في المستقبل

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: The Qāḍī interprets the result as punishment for hypocrisy—grief, constriction, humiliation, and blame lasting into the afterlife; Razi rejects this as an unsupported departure from the apparent sense.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي : المراد من قوله : { فأعقبهم نفاقا فى قلوبهم } أي فأعقبهم العقوبة على النفاق

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth defines أعقبت فلانا ندامة as making regret the outcome; the Hudhaylī poem’s أعقبوني witnesses this sense, also illustrated by food causing illness and God giving someone good.
rows.anchor: قال الليث : يقال : أعقبت فلانا ندامة إذا صيرت عاقبة أمره ذلك . قال الهذلي : أودى بني وأعقبوني حسرة … بعد الرقاد وعبرة لا تقلع

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan al-Baṣrī holds that breaking a pledge and failing a promise necessarily produce hypocrisy; Razi says Muslims should carefully fulfill any pledge to God.
rows.anchor: ومذهب الحسن البصري رحمة الله أنه يوجب النفاق لا محالة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says three traits mark a hypocrite even if the person prays, fasts, and claims faith: lying when speaking, breaking a promise, and betraying a trust.
rows.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( ثلاث من / كن فيه فهو منافق وإن صلى وصام

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet promises Paradise for observing six duties, including truthful speech, keeping promises, honoring trusts, and guarding eyes, hands, and private parts from wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي عليه السلام : ( تقبلوا لي ستا أتقبل لكم الجنة إذا حدثتم فلا تكذبوا

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ reports from Jābir that the Prophet’s three-trait description concerned particular hypocrites who lied to him, betrayed his confidence, and broke their promise to join him.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء بن أبي رباح : حدثني جابر بن عبد الله أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم إنما ذكر قوله ثلاث من

rows.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd reads the traits as lying about God, religion, and the Messenger; breaking the covenant to God; and privately betraying religion while the heart opposes the tongue.
rows.anchor: ونقل أن عمرو بن عبيد فسر الحديث فقال : إذا حدث عن الله كذب عليه وعلى دينه ورسوله

rows.speaker: واصل بن عطاء
rows.claim: Wāṣil ibn ʿAṭāʾ asked al-Ḥasan whether Jacob’s sons were hypocrites because they lied about the wolf, broke their promise to protect Joseph, and betrayed their father’s trust; al-Ḥasan hesitated.
rows.anchor: ونقل أن واصل بن عطاء قال : أتى الحسن رجل فقال له : إن أولاد يعقوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi says Thaʿlaba later brought his charity, but the Prophet said God had forbidden accepting it; no one accepted it before Thaʿlaba died, fulfilling the verse’s prediction that he remained a hypocrite.
rows.anchor: فإنه روي أن ثعلبة أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بصدقته فقال : إن الله تعالى منعني أن أقبل صدقتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report’s agreement with the prediction is evidence of foreknowledge and thus a miracle.
rows.anchor: فدل على أن مخبر هذا الخبر وقع موافقا ، فكان إخبارا عن الغيب فكان معجزا

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī says anthropomorphists use meeting God as proof of vision, but the hypocrites’ meeting cannot mean vision since disbelievers do not see God; a false oath’s meeting God angry likewise means meeting punishment, a case the Qāḍī approves.
rows.anchor: قال الجبائي : إن المشبهة تمسكوا في إثبات رؤية الله تعالى بقوله : { تحيتهم يوم يلقونه سلام }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects that inference: where separate evidence excludes vision in a particular use of meeting, it does not require excluding vision from every other use.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأنا تركنا حمل لفظ اللقاء على الرؤية في هذه الآية ، وفي هذا الخبر لدليل منفصل ، فلم يلزمنا ذلك في سائر الصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Meeting means reaching; seeing an object entails reaching it, so vision can be a kind of meeting, just as إدراك is reaching or overtaking in 26:61.
rows.anchor: لا شك أن اللقاء عبارة عن الوصول ومن رأى شيئا فقد وصل إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here meeting God means encountering His judgment and recompense, as when someone says a person will meet their deed; 9:77 explains this as punishment for breaking the promise and lying.
rows.anchor: بل المقصود أنه تعالى { فى قلوبهم إلى يوم يلقونه } أي حكمه وقضاءه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Secret is what breasts conceal; najwā is private discussion among people, from najwa, a secluded elevation or place, since interlocutors exclude others; Razi links 19:52, 12:80, 58:9, and 58:12.
rows.anchor: والسر ما ينطوي عليه صدورهم ، والنجوى ما يفاوض فيه بعضهم بعضا فيما بينهم ، وهو مأخوذ من النجوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning is that hypocrites dare to conspire despite knowing God sees their hidden and whispered conduct as clearly as the public, and punishes it likewise.
rows.anchor: إذا عرفت الفرق بين السر والنجوى ، فالمقصود من الآية كأنه تعالى قال : ألم يعلموا أن الله يعلم سرهم ونجواهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAllām intensifies ʿālim; the unseen is what creatures cannot perceive, and God’s essence entails knowledge of every thing, including inner thoughts, so nothing can be hidden from Him.
rows.anchor: والعلام مبالغة في العالم ، والغيب ما كان غائبا عن الخلق . والمراد أنه تعالى ذاته تقتضي العلم بجميع الأشياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi compares this divine title with Jesus’ words in 5:116.
rows.anchor: ونظير لفظ علام الغيوب ههنا قول عيسى عليه السلام : { إنك أنت علام الغيوب }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God ʿallāma is improper because the form suggests effortful learning, and effort is impossible for God.
rows.anchor: فأما وصف الله بالعلامة فإنه لا يجوز لأنه مشعر بنوع تكلف فيها يعلم والتكلف في حق الله محال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the two punishments as illnesses in this life and punishment in the afterlife: illness expiates believers’ sins but increases disbelievers’ unbelief and ingratitude.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : يريد الأمراض في الدنيا ، وعذاب الآخرة ، وذلك أن مرض المؤمن يفيده تكفير السيئات

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Al-Suddī reports from Anas that the Prophet publicly ordered named hypocrites out of Friday prayer, exposing them; this was the first punishment, followed by punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: روى السدي عن أنس بن مالك أن النبي عليه السلام قام خطيبا يوم الجمعة فقال : ( اخرج يا فلان فإنك منافق

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies the punishments as worldly killing and captivity, followed by punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد : في الدنيا بالقتل والسبي وبعد ذلك بعذاب القبر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies them as dabīla and grave punishment; the Prophet told Ḥudhayfa that six of twelve hypocrites would die from a fiery lamp-like affliction emerging through the chest, while six would die normally.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة بالدببيلة وعذاب القبر ، وذلك أن النبي عليه السلام أسر إلى حذيفة اثني عشر رجلا من المنافقين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the punishments are taking zakat from their wealth and punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : يأخذ الزكاة من أموالهم ، وعذاب القبر

rows.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq identifies the first punishment as their bitterness at Islam’s advance and their entering Islam without good deeds, followed by grave punishment.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن إسحاق : هو ما يدخل عليهم من غيظ الإسلام ودخولهم فيه من غير حسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unattributed seventh view says angels strike their faces and backs for one punishment, while at resurrection a neck of fire is assigned to them for the other.
rows.anchor: والوجه السابع : أحد العذابين ضرب الملائكة الوجوه والأدبار . والآخر عند البعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers three stages of life: the two punishments are all forms of worldly punishment and grave punishment; the later great torment is the eternal fire of resurrection.
rows.anchor: والأولى أن يقال مراتب الحياة ثلاثة : حياة الدنيا ، وحياة القبر ، وحياة القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two views identify the people who confessed: repentant hypocrites, or Muslims who missed Tabūk through laziness rather than unbelief or hypocrisy, then regretted and repented.
rows.anchor: قوله : { وءاخرون اعترفوا بذنوبهم } فيه قولان : الأول

rows.speaker: قائلون بالقول الأول
rows.claim: Those favoring the first view cite the conjunction with the nearby mention of hypocritical Bedouins: the first group persisted in hypocrisy, while this group was enabled to repent.
rows.anchor: واحتج القائلون بالقول الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report names three men, while another says ten, seven of whom bound themselves in the mosque. The Prophet initially refused to release them without revelation, then freed and excused them; their request that he take their wealth preceded 9:103.
rows.anchor: روي أنهم كانوا ثلاثة : أبو لبابة مروان بن عبد المنذر ، وأوس بن ثعلبة ، ووديعة بن حزام ، وقيل : كانوا عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linguistically, confession is acknowledging something with knowledge; its nuance is that they did not invent excuses but admitted wrongdoing, regretted it, and blamed themselves for staying behind.
rows.anchor: قال أهل اللغة : الاعتراف عبارة عن الإقرار بالشيء عن معرفة ، ومعناه أنهم أقروا بذنبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Confession alone is not repentance; repentance combines regret for the past and resolve to stop in future, with regret because God prohibited the act.
rows.anchor: قلنا : مجرد الاعتراف بالذنب لا يكون توبة ، فأما إذا اقترن به الندم على الماضي ، والعزم على تركه في المستقبل

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Razi says the commentators take God’s use of ʿasā as indicating that their repentance will certainly be accepted.
rows.anchor: والمفسرون قالوا : إن عسى من الله يدل على الوجوب

rows.speaker: الأول
rows.claim: One interpretation makes the good deed their confession, regret, and repentance, and the bad deed their failure to join the expedition.
rows.anchor: الأول : العمل الصالح هو الاعتراف بالذنب والندامة عليه والتوبة منه ، والسيء هو التخلف عن الغزو

rows.speaker: الثاني
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes their good deeds as joining the Messenger on other campaigns and the bad deed as missing Tabūk.
rows.anchor: العمل الصالح خروجهم مع الرسول إلى سائر الغزوات والسيء هو تخلفهم عن غزوة تبوك

rows.speaker: الثالث
rows.claim: A third view says the verse concerns Muslims, and the good deed is the good works they had performed.
rows.anchor: أن هذه الآية نزلت في حق المسلمين كان العمل الصالح إقدامهم على أعمال البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here mixing means simple combination, not intermixture that changes each item’s original quality, as in mixing water and milk.
rows.anchor: واللائق بهذا الموضع هو الجمع المطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi uses the wording to reject cancellation of deeds: obedience retains its praise and reward, sin its blame and punishment; because both are described as mixed, both must remain present, since an attribute cannot exist without its subject.
rows.anchor: فدل على بقاء العملين حال الاختلاط

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say divine ʿasā means certainty, citing 5:52 where the promised victory occurred; human speech conventions let a great ruler use ʿasā to signal that his acts are favor, not an obligation, while still guaranteeing the answer.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون : كلمة عسى من الله واجب ، والدليل عليه قوله تعالى : { فعسى الله أن يأتي بالفتح } ( المائدة : 52 )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer is that ʿasā keeps the person morally responsible in hope and apprehension, discouraging denial and neglect.
rows.anchor: المقصود منه بيان أنه يجب أن يكون المكلف على الطمع والإشفاق لأنه أبعد من الإنكار والإهمال

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: Razi’s school reads this as repentance being created by God: regret is not chosen by the servant, since willing it would require another will and people cannot dismiss either desire or regret at will.
rows.anchor: قال أصحابنا قوله : { عسى الله أن يتوب عليهم } صريح في أن التوبة لا تحصل إلا من خلق الله تعالى

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilites interpret God’s repentance as His accepting the servant’s repentance.
rows.anchor: قالت المعتزلة : المراد من قوله : يتوب الله أنه يقبل توبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the Muʿtazilite interpretation: departing from the apparent meaning is warranted only when proof makes it impossible, whereas reason here supports the apparent reading.
rows.anchor: والجواب : أن الصرف عن الظاهر إنما يحسن ، إذا ثبت بالدليل أنه لا يمكن إجراء اللفظ على ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their confession occurred in the past, while the hoped-for repentance is future; confession therefore preceded and was not itself repentance.
rows.anchor: وذلك يدل على أن ذلك الاعتراف ما كان نفس التوبة ، بل كان مقدمة للتوبة ، وأن التوبة إنما تحصل بعدها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the command concerns repentant men who offered their wealth; taking it completes their repentance like expiation, and it is not obligatory zakat but charity expiating their sin.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن ، وكان يقول ليس المراد من هذه الآية الصدقة الواجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view says zakat was already obligatory; after they repented from missing the expedition, professed Islam sincerely, and offered zakat, the Messenger was ordered to collect it.
rows.anchor: والقول الثاني : أن الزكوات كانت واجبة عليهم

rows.speaker: أكثر الفقهاء
rows.claim: A third view, held by most jurists, treats the passage as a new command to collect zakat from the wealthy; they cite it to establish zakat’s obligation and call zakat purification.
rows.anchor: والقول الثالث : أن هذه الآية كلام مبتدأ ، والمقصود منها إيجاب أخذ الزكاة من الأغنياء وعليه أكثر الفقهاء

rows.speaker: القائلون بالقول الأول
rows.claim: Those favoring expiatory charity argue that a fresh zakat command would break the coherence with surrounding verses and leave this one unrelated to what precedes and follows.
rows.anchor: احتجوا على صحة قولهم بأن الآيات لا بد وأن تكون منتظمة متناسقة

rows.speaker: القائلون بالقول الثاني
rows.claim: Defenders of obligatory zakat preserve the link: the men admitted love of wealth had caused their absence, so paying zakat willingly tests whether their repentance is sincere; refusal exposes them as liars.
rows.anchor: فكأنه قيل لهم إنما يظهر صحة قولكم في ادعاء هذه التوبة والندامة لو أخرجتم الزكاة الواجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers obligatory zakat because purification from sin by taking the charity fits only an obligation: sin would result if they failed to pay what was due.
rows.anchor: وهذا إنما يصح لو قلنا إنه لو لم يأخذ تلك الصدقة لحصل الذنب ، وذلك إنما يصح حصوله في الصدقات الواجبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the men offered wealth to seek purification and forgiveness; the Prophet initially said he had no order to take it, then took one-third and left two-thirds after revelation. مِن indicates a portion, and Razi says the report still fits his preferred view because willingness to give optional charity makes willingness to pay obligations more fitting.
rows.anchor: فأنزل الله تعالى هذه الآيات فأخذ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ثلث أموالهم ، وترك الثلثين لأنه تعالى قال : { خذ من أموالهم صدقة } ولم يقل خذ أموالهم
